passage:
Outside the tuition class in the small town, an older boy called Kunal leaned on his bike and held out a packet. "Free. Take it. Everyone at the river ghat hangs out with me, you can too."
Farida had watched him hand things to younger kids all month, and she had heard he asked one of them to hold some packets for him. Her stomach turned. "No, thanks," she said, and walked straight to Nandini, her cousin waiting by the tea stall.
"He gives free stuff so people owe him," Nandini muttered. Neither of them looked back.
That evening Farida told her mother, who called the tuition teacher, and the teacher spoke to the school head. Farida felt shaky, but not ashamed.

qa.q: Where was Nandini waiting when Farida walked away from Kunal?
qa.a: Nandini was waiting by the tea stall.

qa.q: How was Farida feeling when Kunal held out the packet?
qa.a: Her stomach turned, so she felt uneasy and suspicious because she had watched him hand things to younger kids and heard he asked one to hold packets.

qa.q: What did Farida do that shows she recognised the hook?
qa.a: She said no and walked away, then told her mother, who called the tuition teacher, and the teacher spoke to the school head.

qa.q: What does Nandini think the free things are for?
qa.a: Nandini muttered that he gives free stuff so people owe him, which shows Nandini sees it as a way of binding younger kids to him.

grounding: Shows a teen recognising an older boy's free offers as a hook, refusing, leaving and telling an adult.

passage: Coach's log, Thursday, under-16 football. After practice I saw Tejas, the older lad who hangs around the ground, walk Ujjwal to the gate and press something into his hand. Ujjwal handed it straight back, shook his head and walked back towards the pavilion instead of leaving with him. Ten minutes later he found me by the kit bags. He said Tejas had been giving free vapes to a few of the juniors for weeks and had now asked him to 'carry a few packets to school, easy money.' His voice was shaking. I told him he had done exactly the right thing, that none of this was on him, and stayed with him while I rang the school's safeguarding lead, Mrs Fernandes. She came to the ground within the hour, spoke with Ujjwal and called his parents in that evening. We are reporting Tejas's visits to the police and the ground manager.

qa.q: What did Tejas ask Ujjwal to do?
qa.a: He asked him to carry a few packets to school, calling it easy money.

qa.q: What does Ujjwal's shaking voice suggest?
qa.a: He was frightened and nervous about reporting an older boy, but determined enough to do it anyway.

qa.q: What did the coach's response get right?
qa.a: The coach said it was not Ujjwal's fault, stayed with him and brought in the safeguarding lead the same day.

qa.q: How might Tejas see the free vapes he handed out?
qa.a: He likely sees them as bait to pull juniors into his circle and get them carrying packets for him.

grounding: A coach's note showing a teen recognise an older lad's free vapes as a hook, refuse, leave and tell a trusted adult.

passage: Tuesday night. Diary, today was weird. Ramesh from Class 12 stopped me near the cycle stand and held out a strip of pills and a box of sweets. 'Free, Tushar. Makes exam stress vanish. Come sit with us at lunch.' Then he said if I liked them, I could sell a few to the Class 9 kids and keep some for myself. That's when my stomach went cold. Nobody gives stuff away free. It's a hook, to get me owing him. I said, 'No thanks, I'm late for tuition,' and cycled off fast. At dinner I told Papa everything. He put his roti down, said I'd done nothing wrong and he was glad I walked away. He called Principal ma'am right then, and she said she will speak to the school counsellor and to Ramesh's parents tomorrow morning. I feel lighter now. Still a bit scared of seeing Ramesh at the stand.

qa.q: What did Ramesh hold out to Tushar near the cycle stand?
qa.a: He held out a strip of pills and a box of sweets.

qa.q: What was Tushar feeling when Ramesh mentioned selling to the Class 9 kids?
qa.a: Tushar felt a cold jolt of alarm, sensing the free offer was a hook meant to leave Tushar owing Ramesh.

qa.q: What would you advise Tushar to do if Ramesh approaches again?
qa.a: Keep saying no, move towards other people, and tell Papa or the counsellor straight away.

qa.q: How does Papa see what Tushar told him?
qa.a: Papa takes it seriously and is glad Tushar walked away, so he calls the principal that same evening.

grounding: A diary showing a teen recognise an older student's free pills as a hook, refuse, leave and tell a parent the same day.
